procedural_history.originating_court: First Grade as Senior Sub-Judge, Gurgaon, in Suit No. 35 of 1940-41
procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Decree, dated the 29th August, 1944, of the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad (Mulla and Yorke JJ.)
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The High Court reversed the decree of the trial court, holding that the defendants are entitled to 4/5th share as proprietors, that the original agreement repeated in subsequent Settlements was binding on the parties so long as the Settlements were in force, that it ceased to have any effect after the expiry of the Settlements and that the renewal of its terms in the Settlement of 1938-39 was not binding as they were not agreed to by the contesting defendants.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The defendants appealed to the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court allowed the appeal, set aside the decree of the High Court, and restored the decree of the trial court.

decision.appeal_result: For. the reasons given above we allow the appeal, set aside the decree of the High Court decreeing the plaintiff's suit and restore the decree of the trial Court dismissing· the plaintiff's suit. In the circumstances of this case we will make no order as to costs.

issue.issue_text: Whether an entry regarding an agreement in a Wajib-ul-arz holds good and remains operative after the expiry of the period of the Settlement in which it was made.

facts: An agreement prohibiting the partition of property was recorded in the Wajib-ul-arz during the Settlements of 1877 and 1908-09.
These Settlement periods had expired by the time of the lawsuit.
The defendants, who were previously bound by this agreement, were now seeking partition of the property.
law: The established legal principle, supported by several prior court cases (Hira and Others v. Muhamadi and Others; Allah Bakhsh and Others v. Mirza Bashir-ud-Din and Others; Lieut. Chaudhri Chattar Singh v. Mt. Shugni and Another), is that an entry regarding an agreement in a Wajib-ul-arz is only valid for the duration of the Settlement in which it was made.
application: The Supreme Court applied this legal principle directly to the facts of the case.
It reasoned that the agreement prohibiting partition was not intended to be perpetual but was limited to the period of the specific Settlement in which it was recorded.
Since the Settlements of 1877 and 1908-09 had ceased to operate, the agreement recorded within them also became inoperative.
Consequently, the Court found there was no legal reason to continue enforcing the prohibition against partition against the defendants.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court decided that an entry regarding an agreement in a Wajib-ul-arz holds good only during the currency of the Settlement in which it was made and does not survive the expiry of that period. Therefore, the old agreement was no longer a bar to the defendants' claim for partition.

issue.issue_text: Whether the plea of adverse possession could arise when possession was under an arrangement between co-sharers.

facts: The parties involved were co-sharers in the property.
The possession of the property was governed by an arrangement between these co-sharers, which was recorded in settlement papers.
The appellants claimed they had acquired title by adverse possession for over 50 years.
law: Possession that is permissive, such as under an arrangement between co-owners, cannot be considered adverse.
Adverse possession requires possession to be hostile to the true owner's rights.
application: The Supreme Court affirmed the decision of the High Court.
The High Court had determined that the possession of the property was based on an arrangement between the co-sharers.
Because the possession was by agreement among co-owners, it was not hostile.
The court found that the evidence, including settlement papers, consistently showed joint ownership, which supported the existence of a permissive arrangement rather than adverse possession.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court rejected the plea of adverse possession, holding that since the possession was under an arrangement between co-sharers, it was permissive and not hostile, and therefore the question of adverse possession could not arise.

issue.issue_text: Whether a will made by a father in favour of his daughter should be presumed to grant only a limited life estate.

facts: A will was made by a father in favour of his daughter.
A lower court (the High Court) held that because the will was from a father to a daughter, it should be presumed that the father only intended to grant her a limited life estate, not full ownership.
law: There is no legal presumption that a will made by a father for his daughter is intended to grant only a limited life estate.
To convey full rights of ownership in a will, it is not necessary to explicitly grant the power of alienation.
It is sufficient if the words used in the will are of such 'amplitude' (i.e., broad enough) as to convey full ownership rights.
application: The Supreme Court applied this legal principle to the High Court's decision.
It found that the High Court was 'clearly wrong in law' for starting with the presumption that only a limited estate was granted.

The correct approach is to examine the language of the will itself to see if the words used are broad enough to grant full ownership, rather than relying on a presumption based on the relationship between the testator (father) and the beneficiary (daughter).
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court rejected the High Court's view, holding that there is no legal presumption that a will from a father to a daughter grants only a limited life estate. The court ruled that the High Court was wrong to apply such a presumption.

arguments.issue_text: Whether an entry regarding an agreement in a Wajib-ul-arz holds good and remains operative after the expiry of the period of the Settlement in which it was made.
appellant_arguments: The appellant's argument, by inference from their appeal against the High Court's decision, is that the agreement recorded in the Settlement documents continued to be binding even after the expiry of the Settlements.
respondent_arguments: The original agreement was only binding so long as the Settlements were in force and ceased to have any effect after their expiry.
The renewal of the agreement's terms in the subsequent Settlement of 1938-39 was not binding as they had not agreed to it.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the plea of adverse possession could arise when possession was under an arrangement between co-sharers.
appellant_arguments: The appellants had acquired title by adverse possession over the defendants' share for more than 50 years.
respondent_arguments: The possession was under an arrangement between the co-sharers, and therefore, no question of adverse possession could arise.

arguments.issue_text: Whether a will made by a father in favour of his daughter should be presumed to grant only a limited life estate.
appellant_arguments: The will conveyed full rights of ownership, as it is not necessary to give express powers of alienation; using words of sufficient amplitude to convey full ownership is enough.
respondent_arguments: A will made by a father in favour of his daughter should be presumed to grant only a limited life estate.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: When a right of pre-emption rests upon custom, it becomes the law of the place (lex loci) and attaches to the land itself, affecting all lands in that place irrespective of the religion, nationality, or domicile of the owners, unless such incidents are proven to be a part of the custom itself. An entry regarding an agreement in a Wajib-ul-arz is operative only for the duration of the Settlement period in which it is made and becomes inoperative when the Settlement ends. To convey full rights of ownership, it is not necessary that specific words of alienation be used; it is sufficient if the words used are of such amplitude as would convey full ownership.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The High Court was clearly wrong in law to presume that a will made by a father in favour of his daughter granted only a limited life estate. It is not necessary for a will to give express powers of alienation to convey full ownership; it is sufficient if the words used are of such amplitude as would convey full rights of ownership. This erroneous interpretation of the will was the dispositive issue that led to the reversal of the High Court's decree.
legal_tests_applied: An entry regarding an agreement in a Wajib-ul-arz holds good only during the period of the Settlement in which it is made and becomes inoperative when the Settlement has come to an end.
A plea of adverse possession cannot arise when possession is held under an arrangement between co-sharers.
To convey full rights of ownership, a will does not need to give express powers of alienation; it is enough if words of sufficient amplitude are used.
Partition is a right incident to the ownership of property.
why_appellant_lost: The appellant's argument that the agreement in the Wajib-ul-arz remained operative was rejected because the court found the agreement was not for perpetuity but for a limited period only, becoming inoperative when the Settlement ended.

The appellant's plea of acquiring title by adverse possession was rejected because the court affirmed the High Court's finding that possession was under an arrangement between the co-sharers, and therefore no question of adverse possession could arise.
why_respondent_won: The respondent successfully argued that the agreement in the Wajib-ul-arz ceased to have any effect after the expiry of the Settlements, a position the court accepted by stating the agreement was for a limited period and became inoperative when the Settlement came to an end.

The respondent successfully defeated the plea of adverse possession by establishing that the possession was permissive. The court agreed that because possession was under an arrangement between co-sharers, the plea had no substance.
policy_considerations: Partition is a right incident to the ownership of property and once parties are held as co-owners, their right to partition cannot be resisted.
